attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary, 10.100.153.10), node2, and node3 (replicas), with all replication traffic carried over TLS and gated by a cluster-specific CA. Generated a CA and per-node server certs plus a client cert (CN=replicator) on node1, distributed via an ephemeral HTTP transfer (no SSH daemon available), installed certs into each node's /etc/postgresql/16/main, enabled ssl=on with wal_level=replica, and restricted pg_hba.conf on node1 to `hostssl replication replicator <peer-ip>/32 cert clientcert=verify-full` for node2/node3 IPs only. Took pg_basebackup -R base backups from node1 (sslmode=verify-full) to seed node2/node3 as standbys; both came up streaming with pg_stat_replication showing ssl=t and client_dn=/CN=replicator. Verified a cert signed by a different (untrusted) CA is rejected with 'unknown ca'. Verified write propagation of an inserted row to both replicas. Completed the mandatory rolling-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id baselines, restarted node3, node2, then primary node1 (one at a time, replicas first so an independent recovery path/read access remained available throughout), confirmed each node's boot_id changed, confirmed each node's PostgreSQL/replication role recovered (recovery mode + pg_stat_replication rows for standbys; ssl=on + reconnected replicas for primary), and confirmed data (including a post-restart insert) is present on all replicas.
